what_its_for: Podofilox is used to treat genital warts (also called condyloma acuminata) that are on the outside of your body. It works by destroying the wart tissue. This medicine does NOT cure the virus that causes warts, and warts may come back after treatment.
how_to_take: Podofilox comes as a liquid solution (applied with a cotton swab) or a gel (applied with your finger). Always wash your hands before and after applying this medicine. Use a cotton swab or your finger to apply a small amount ONLY to the wart tissue — try your best NOT to get it on the healthy skin around the wart. Let the area dry completely before putting on clothing. Do NOT use more than directed, and do NOT apply it inside your vagina, anus, mouth, or eyes.
dosing: Apply podofilox to your warts TWICE a day (morning and evening) for 3 days in a row. Then stop using it for 4 days. This 3-days-on, 4-days-off schedule counts as ONE treatment cycle. You may repeat up to 4 cycles total (about 4 weeks). Do NOT use more than 0.5 mL of solution per day. Talk to your doctor if warts are still there after 4 cycles.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember on that same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do NOT apply extra medicine to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store podofilox at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, open flames, and direct sunlight, as it is flammable. Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do NOT freeze it.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT use podofilox on warts inside the vagina, cervix, rectum, or mouth — it is only for external (outside) use. Avoid getting it on healthy skin, as it can cause irritation and damage. Do NOT have sexual contact while the medicine is on your skin, and consider using a condom during treatment. Avoid letting anyone else use your medicine. Do NOT use near open flames or while smoking, as the solution is flammable.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you notice: severe pain, burning, or bleeding at the treatment site; signs of infection such as increased redness, swelling, warmth, or pus; sores or open wounds that do not heal; warts getting much worse or spreading; dizziness, nausea, or vomiting; or if warts are still present after 4 treatment cycles. Seek emergency help if you accidentally swallow any of this medicine.
when_it_works: You may start to notice that warts begin to shrink or change appearance within the first week or two of treatment. Most people see results after completing several treatment cycles (up to 4 weeks). Some people may need additional treatments prescribed by their doctor if warts do not fully go away.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT use podofilox if you are pregnant or think you may be pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant during treatment. Breastfeeding: It is not known if podofilox passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are breastfeeding. Children: The safety and effectiveness of podofilox in children under 18 have not been established. Older adults: Use with caution; follow your doctor's instructions closely.
